_comment: Read registry for the social content pipeline. Maps the Notion content databases to the Google Drive media tree, and holds the folder-naming convention as data rather than as a literal buried in an automation. Consumed by content-ingest-agent, scripts/content_media_select.py and .claude/commands/content-schedule.md. Source: live Notion + Drive reads, 2026-09-12.
_maintenance: Two things go stale independently. (1) Notion property names are EXACT MATCH — a rename in Notion silently breaks reads; re-verify with notion-fetch on the data_source url. (2) drive.root_folder_id is pinned deliberately: there are three folders in this account whose title contains 'Titan Flooring', one of them shared by an external agency (kim@socialestatesmarketing.com). NEVER resolve the root by title search — always by id.

titan_content_ideas._comment: The planning database. One row per content item; 'Next: Post To' selects the platform for the next post, and Content Calendar Log records each post that went out.
titan_content_ideas._id_property_comment: Auto-increment. This integer is the join key to the Drive folder (ID 170 <-> folder TC-170_...), which is why no extra cross-reference field is needed.
titan_content_ideas._schema_verified: 2026-09-12: 8 properties added live, TikTok added to 'Next: Post To'. 14 rows carrying 'Instagram Reels' verified intact after the ALTER.

write_properties._comment: The ONLY properties any part of this pipeline may write. Everything else on the row is Albert's and the team's. Mirrors the read/write split in pricelist-sources.json.

titan_content_ideas._never_write: Never write Status, Next: Post To, Caption, Post Date or Link to Files. Those are the plan; the pipeline reports against them and does not edit them. An agent that 'corrects' Next: Post To has decided what to post, which is the one thing it must never do.

content_calendar_log._comment: Append-only posting history. One row per platform per content item — this is the fan-out record, not a duplicate of the idea.

drive._comment: Google Drive is the media source of record as of 2026-09-12, replacing SharePoint/OneDrive. Chosen because Metricool auto-ingests Drive URLs natively: no Graph permission to widen, no pre-authenticated-URL expiry, and none of the FedAuth cookie problem that makes a raw SharePoint share link unusable to a third party (see scripts/pricelist_fetch.py).
drive._sharing_requirement: Every asset handed to Metricool MUST be shared anyone-with-link/viewer, or the fetch 404s. A link that opens in Albert's signed-in browser proves nothing -- verify signed out.
drive._verified: 2026-09-13: root confirmed as the folder Make writes into, holding TC-165_QA How Much Does Flooring Installation Cost in the GTA.
drive._share_scope_comment: Share the 03_FINAL folder (or the individual asset), NEVER root_folder_id. Drive permissions inherit, so sharing the root would be simpler -- and would expose every 01_RAW folder, i.e. raw unedited footage inside clients' homes, to anyone holding the link. Finished assets are already destined for public social feeds, so link-sharing those costs nothing; raw footage is not, and was never consented to for publication. Narrower is correct here even though it means the Make scenario shares per item rather than once.
drive._no_credential: This repo holds NO Google credential and needs none. Drive reads go through the user-delegated Drive MCP connector, held by /content-schedule and content-ingest-agent. scripts/content_media_select.py deliberately does no I/O -- it takes a folder listing and returns a choice or a refusal. A service account was considered and rejected: it would not see Albert's personal My Drive without per-file sharing, so it would add a credential to guard without removing any work.
drive._root_folder_id_comment: REPOINTED 2026-09-13. TWO folders named 'Titan Flooring Content' exist under TITAN FLOORING, created ten minutes apart: 1rbFy6aNyb1PXjAEIvOhZyZNK4bvpUBCq (20:02, empty) and this one (20:12). The Make scenario writes into THIS one -- TC-165_... is here. The registry originally pinned the empty duplicate: the id was taken from a title search at a moment when only one existed, which is why pinning an id is necessary but not sufficient when the NAME is ambiguous at pin time. Verify a pinned id still holds what you expect, do not just check that it is an id. Albert to delete the empty duplicate so this cannot recur.

folder_convention._comment: The per-content-item scaffold. Created by the Make scenario on a new Notion row; read by the resolver. Holding the prefix here is the whole point of this block — it was previously a hardcoded literal inside a ~366KB Make blueprint, which is why changing it looked bigger than it was.
folder_convention._legacy_comment: Pre-2026-09-12 folders are TFC-<n>, and some are TFC<n> with no separator at all (TFC-168_VALUE.m4a alongside TFC167_VALUE.m4a). Both are normalised to TC-<n> during the migration. 'TC' is not a substring of 'TFC', so the two prefixes can never match each other by accident and a half-migrated estate stays unambiguous.
folder_convention._match_comment: Resolve by the integer, tolerating any known prefix and an optional separator. Never match on the prefix itself — it is decoration and it is changing.
folder_convention._media_dir_comment: The single source of postable assets. The pipeline reads ONLY this. Raw footage in 01_RAW is 99.3% of the tree's bytes and is never touched.
folder_convention._scaffold_comment: UNIFORM for every Content Format (Albert, 2026-09-13), replacing the old per-format branching. Content Format is an EDITABLE property: a row switched from Shortform to Carasoul after its folders exist would leave a tree that no longer matches, and nothing reconciles it. Making the scaffold a function of nothing means it cannot drift. It also removes the format branch from the Make scenario, which is most of why the old one needed 28 createAFolder modules. Cost accepted: an Image row gets 30_INSTALL it will never use.

_dropped_from_the_old_scaffold.02_SELECTS: chosen clips are an editing artifact -> 02_EDIT
_dropped_from_the_old_scaffold.03_AUDIO: same material as voiceover, and it is source -> 01_RAW/70_VOICEOVER
_dropped_from_the_old_scaffold.04_PHOTOS: photos are captured, so they are raw -> 01_RAW/80_PHOTOS

folder_convention._final_dir_is_flat: 03_FINAL takes no subfolders, ever. content_media_select.py reads files directly from it and would refuse a subfoldered one as empty_final_dir. This is a contract, not a preference.

carousel._comment: Several images and no video in 03_FINAL is a carousel. Slide order must be declared in the filenames -- alphabetical is wrong ('10.jpg' sorts before '9.jpg'), creation time is wrong (slides get re-exported), and guessing publishes the sequence wrong in a way that reads as a design choice rather than a bug, so nobody reports it.
carousel._refusals: carousel_unordered (any slide unnumbered), carousel_gap (gap or two slides claiming one position), carousel_too_long (over max_slides)
carousel._no_cover: A carousel never carries a cover: the first slide is the cover, and Metricool's cover fields apply only to video -- sending one rejects the entire post.

migration._comment: One-time OneDrive -> Drive move, decided 2026-09-12 (Albert). Everything migrates: Drive is a 2TB plan, so 200GB is not a capacity constraint and a single source of truth beats a split archive.
migration._risk: Throughput, not cost. A 51GB folder through Drive's API will throttle. The job must be resumable and idempotent, keyed on notion_id, reporting per row rather than going silent for hours.
migration._safety: Nothing is deleted from OneDrive until Albert confirms the Drive copy is complete and correct. Reversible-by-inaction is the only safe shape at this volume.
migration._notion_rewrite: Every migrated row's 'Link to Files' must be rewritten to the Drive link in the same pass. A moved folder whose Notion row still points at OneDrive is a broken row.

make_scenario._comment: The Make scenario that builds a content item's Drive scaffold, nests it under its Notion parent, and writes the folder link back to the row. ONE scenario -- it drives its own recursion by re-firing its own webhook. Ids live here, never in a blueprint or a prompt.
make_scenario.name: Content Status -> Create Drive Folders (v2)
make_scenario._shape: webhook -> datastore Exist -> Notion get item -> datastore Get parent -> Router{ parent unknown: POST self for the parent, POST self again with attempt+1, stop | parent known: create TC-<n>_<name> under it, AddRecord, scaffold x4, share 03_FINAL, write Link to Files, iterate the nine 01_RAW children }
make_scenario._why_queue_and_refire: Make has no loop or recursion primitive, and a blocking filter stops the WHOLE downstream branch, so 'look up the parent, build it if missing, then carry on' is not expressible inline. The obvious answer -- call your own webhook and WAIT for the folder id -- holds depth+2 executions open at once, all idle-waiting, and cannot be serialised without deadlocking (an execution would wait on a nested one that can never start). Firing and forgetting instead means nothing ever waits on anything, which is what makes sequential processing safe, which is what makes the sibling race impossible. The cost is that a deep chain resolves over several queued fires across a few seconds instead of in one call.
make_scenario._sequential_comment: MUST stay true. Two sibling rows firing at once would both find their shared parent missing and both create it, leaving two identically-named parent folders with one child in each and the datastore pointing at whichever finished last -- silent, and nobody notices until someone goes looking for footage. Serialising removes the race outright. It is only safe because no execution blocks on another; do not combine it with a design that waits.
make_scenario._max_attempts_comment: Runaway guard. Each re-fire of a row carries attempt+1; past this the row is dropped at the filter instead of queueing again, so a relation cycle cannot loop forever. The deepest real chain in Notion today is 3 levels (TC-48 '1060 Britannia' -> TC-51 'Warehouse Layout' -> 'Shortform: Satisfying All Parties + Myself'), which is why a fixed depth-2 unroll was never an option.
make_scenario._status_gate_is_entry_only: LOAD-BEARING, and non-obvious. The Planning/Filming gate applies ONLY to calls originating from Notion. A self-call is recognised by carrying an `attempt` field and bypasses it, because a PARENT must be buildable regardless of its own Status -- otherwise a parent still in 'Idea' can never get a folder and every chain through it stalls.

nesting._comment: Drive mirrors Notion's Parent item / Sub-item tree. A child's content folder sits DIRECTLY inside its parent's content folder, alongside 01_RAW..04_PUBLISHED -- so a parent's folder holds a mix of scaffold folders and child folders. Intended.
nesting._same_data_source: Parent item is a SELF-relation on Titan Content Ideas, so a parent is always a row in the same data source and always has its own ID/Content Name. No out-of-database ancestor is reachable, so no data-source check is needed. Verified 2026-09-13: the apparent 'hub page' TC-48 '1060 Britannia' is an ordinary content row with 7 sub-items.
nesting._implicit_parents: A parent created because a child fired first gets IDENTICAL treatment to one triggered directly: full scaffold, 03_FINAL shared, Link to Files written.
nesting._multiple_parents: Parent item is an array. Every row today has exactly one; the build takes the first. A second parent would be silently ignored.

datastore._key_comment: Keyed on the Notion PAGE ID, not TC-<n>. The Parent item relation hands back the parent's page id directly, so a parent lookup is one datastore read with no extra Notion fetch. Page ids are immutable, where the ID prefix has already changed once (TFC -> TC). contentID stores the Drive FOLDER ID, so a record answers *where*, not just *whether*.
datastore._root_sentinel_comment: LOAD-BEARING DATA, not test junk -- do not delete it, and re-seed it after any 'delete all records'. This one record is the recursion's base case: a row with no parent looks up '__ROOT__' and the datastore answers with the Drive root folder id, exactly like any other parent lookup. Without it, 'has a parent' and 'has no parent' become two router branches, and because a Make filter stops everything downstream, EACH branch would need its own copy of the whole build chain -- the 28-module unrolling that made the predecessor undebuggable. It also keeps the root folder id out of the blueprint entirely. root_sentinel_value MUST equal drive.root_folder_id; if they drift, every folder is created in the wrong place and nothing errors.
datastore._sentinel_cannot_collide: '__ROOT__' is not a valid Notion page id (those are 8-4-4-4-12 hex UUIDs), so the sentinel can never be mistaken for a real row.
datastore._ordering_invariant: AddRecord runs IMMEDIATELY after the content-folder create, before the scaffold. If a scaffold create fails later, the folder exists AND the record exists, so a re-fire is a no-op. Recording after the scaffold would leave a folder with no record, and the next fire would build a duplicate.

fields.contentID: Drive folder ID of this row's content folder
fields.label: human-readable TC-<n>_<name>; nothing reads it

datastore._label_field_comment: Added 2026-09-14. The key is a Notion page id, which is unreadable at a glance, and that unreadability led to the key being hand-changed to TC-<n> three times -- each time silently disabling nesting. `label` gives the record a legible name WITHOUT touching the key. It is written from the created folder's own name ({{8.name}}) and read by nobody.
datastore._why_the_key_cannot_be_TC_n: Notion's `Parent item` relation returns PAGE IDS. A child has no way to learn its parent's TC-<n> without a second Notion fetch, so a datastore keyed on TC-<n> can never be found by the child that needs it. The failure is silent and specific: parentless rows still build at the root and the duplicate guard still works -- only nested rows break, burning max_attempts passes each and ending with no folder and no error. Verified live 2026-09-13: TC-152 correctly resolved its parent to page id 35b596a4-..., missed a datastore holding 'TC-59', and re-queued itself.

share._comment: The predecessor shared with role 'writer' -- anyone holding the link could edit or delete -- on a folder above 01_RAW, which is raw unedited footage inside clients' homes. Share 03_FINAL only, read-only.

_defects_fixed_2026_09_13: Make's filter `conditions` is an OR of ANDs: the OUTER array is OR, the INNER is AND. Written inverted, [[Planning, Filming]] meant 'Planning AND Filming' and could never be true -- the scenario silently processed nothing (a run consuming exactly 1 operation is the signature).
datastore:ExistRecord outputs `exist`, NOT `exists`. A filter on {{N.exists}} never resolves, so the already-built guard never blocks and every re-fire duplicates the entire folder tree.
A hand-edit had AddRecord keying on TC-<n> while the lookup keyed on page id, and storing the row's TITLE in contentID where a Drive folder id belongs. Never executed.

_confirmed_not_assumed.createAFolder_webViewLink: Confirmed present in the module output schema AND in a live run sample, in the correct https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/<id> form. Never map the share module's `shareLink`, which the Drive app emits in the malformed /folder/d/<id> form.
_confirmed_not_assumed.properties_value_ID: notion:getADatabaseItem exposes named properties under `properties_value`, and ID is the object {prefix, number} -- so the folder name reads .prefix and .number. Note this shape DIFFERS from the raw webhook payload's properties.ID.unique_id.number.

_superseded.name: Create Google Drive Content Folder
_superseded._comment: The unrolled 28-createAFolder predecessor, ~366KB of blueprint. Inactive. Retire it in the Make UI -- never via scenarios_update, which fails silently on a large blueprint (platform-settings/lightspeed.json:132).

make_scenario._status: BUILT AND VERIFIED AS A BLUEPRINT, NEVER FIRED under this design. isActive: false as of 2026-09-13. Do not describe it as working until a real fire is observed -- in particular the re-fire test, which is the direct check on the exist/exists defect above.
